subject: GPU SKU guidance for Novamed dedicated capacity — H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs and action plan
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novamed.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novamed requirements and ask — guidance on H100/A100/L4 for Dedicated

Hi Irene and Dev,

We are finalizing requirements for a dedicated inference deployment for our clinical-chat product and need Redwood's SKU guidance. High-level:
- Steady-state: ~75 qps peak, 24/7 daytime traffic with nightly dips.
- P95 latency target: <120ms for short chat turns (~200 tokens), occasional long-context analysis up to 32k tokens for batch jobs.
- Memory needs: models with a 40–80B footprint for the long-context pipeline; embeddings separate.
- Budget: aiming to keep steady-state costs predictable — willing to reserve capacity for SLAs.

Specific ask: your recommendation between H100, A100 and L4 for Dedicated (reserve+burst) and quick notes on fallback/tiling, caching, and expected tradeoffs. Also: what pilot footprint should we commit to for a 6-week evaluation?

Thanks — Ari
Ari Kaplan
Dir., ML Infrastructure — Novamed
ari.kaplan@novamed.com
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novamed.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed requirements and ask — guidance on H100/A100/L4 for Dedicated

Ari — thanks for the clear summary. 

Quick clarifying questions before we put a concrete SKU map together:
- What percent of requests are short interactive turns vs long-context batch (rough estimate)?
- Are long-context runs latency-sensitive or can they be scheduled/queued?
- Any regulatory constraint on model residency or hardware (e.g., on-prem vs VPC-only)?

We can prepare a recommended reserve+burst mix and a 6-week pilot sizing once we have that breakdown. Tentative approach: hybrid pool — L4s for majority short-turn traffic, H100s for memory-bound long-context, and a small number of A100s as a memory-capacity hedge for peak concurrency. I will loop in Dev for numbers.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: irene.chooi@redwood.ai, Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novamed.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed requirements and ask — guidance on H100/A100/L4 for Dedicated

Ari — putting some concrete numbers on the hybrid approach. Based on similar deployments: 

Short summary:
- L4 (cost-efficient, good for short stateless chat): target ~60–70% of steady qps. Best when requests are <=1k tokens and latency SLOs need to be met cheaply. Quantization + token caching yields large $/token savings.
- H100 (best raw throughput and mixed precision perf): use for long-context (>=8k) and heavy batch post-processing. H100 is our recommended primary for memory-bound 40–80B models when you need concurrency and lowest end-to-end latency for big contexts.
- A100 (memory-density fallback): keep a small reserved pool of A100s for the rare highest-memory, mid-latency-concurrency cases or as a spot fallback for H100 maintenance windows. A100 still matters if you need maximum stable VRAM per process without reliance on newer runtimes.

Pilot sizing (6-week):
- Reserve: 4 x H100 (covers baseline long-context throughput + test load), 6 x L4 (front-door short-turn capacity)
- Burst: add policy to scale up 2–4 A100-equivalents or additional H100 slots for peak test days.
- Observability: enable token-level cost dashboards and per-model tail-latency alerts.

Estimated pilot throughput coverage: ~70 qps with room for bursts to 140 qps for short durations. We will tune autoscaling policies and suggest conservative batch sizes for H100 to balance latency and $/token.

I'll attach a quick worksheet and run the cost model for Novamed numbers if you share short/long request split.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-04T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed requirements and ask — guidance on H100/A100/L4 for Dedicated

Adding operational constraints and rollout advice: 

- Routing policy: route by request type (stateless short vs stateful long). Use L4 pool for short-turns with low-latency routing; H100 pool for stateful long-contexts. Implement automatic fallback to A100s if H100 capacity constrained.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for conversational sessions — this often halves H100 token generation cost for multi-turn flows.
- Quantization: for experimental models, we can recommend int8/4 quant profiles on L4 for short-turn models to reduce memory and increase slot density.
- Safety net: define a failover policy that serves degraded but safe responses from a smaller quantized model on L4 in case of H100 outage.

Procurement and pricing note for the pilot: we should propose a month-by-month pilot commitment with a 10% pilot discount and clear conversion path to a 12-month reserved plan if SLOs and latency meet Novamed's acceptance criteria.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

Ari / Procurement — attaching a short mutual action plan (MAA) and a first-draft SKU map for the 6-week pilot. Attachment: Novamed_MAA_v1.pdf (pilot scope, success criteria, and pilot-reserve recommendations). Key points in the draft: 

1) Pilot commit (6 weeks): reserve 4 H100 + 6 L4. We include autoscaling to add 2 A100-equivalents for burst testing.
2) Success metrics: P95 <120ms for short-turns, stable batch throughput for 32k jobs with completion within agreed window.
3) Observability: token cost dashboard, tail-latency tracking, and a weekly sync.
4) Next steps: Procurement to confirm pilot PO; Engineering to provide short/long split telemetry sample (CSV) by Oct 9.

Please review the attached and let us know edits. We can run a cost modeling pass once we get your telemetry sample.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
